title: Axis-order swap and boundary arithmetic demo
input_data: Three EPSG:4326-style points (Tokyo, Reykjavik, Sydney) as (lat,lon); antimeridian query box lon [179.999, 180.0] against a point stored at -180.0005; float32 narrowing of 179.99995
code_summary: Haversine distance (R=6371008.8 m spherical approximation) between true (lat,lon) and axis-swapped reading; naive vs wrap-normalised bounding-box membership; struct-based float32 narrowing
expected_behavior: Swapped readings silently displace points by thousands of km (|lat|>90 cases are detectable); naive antimeridian test misses a physically-in-box point; float32 narrowing changes the edge value
result_stdout_excerpt: Tokyo: true (35.6762,139.6503) vs swapped (139.6503,35.6762) -> 6471 km displaced, SILENT; Reykjavik -> 12007 km, SILENT; Sydney -> 6988 km, SILENT; W1b: stored as -180.0005 -> naive test False (MISS); wrap-normalised 179.9995 -> True (HIT); W1c: lon 179.99995 -> float32 179.9999542236328
honest_notes: A stray literal 'exit_code_placeholder' line was printed at the end of stdout (authoring artifact in the demo code; it does not affect the numeric assertions and is part of the receipted stdout_sha256).
scope_limits: Isolated component check in the admitted sandbox; spherical-Earth approximation; pure arithmetic only. Does NOT establish any FieldBook application behavior, nor full transform-engine correctness.

title: Field-level three-way merge vs last-writer-wins demo
input_data: Synthetic observation base {taxon 'Fagus sylvatica', height_m 12, note ''}, local {height 15, note 'bark canker seen'}, remote {taxon 'Fagus orientalis', height 14}; plus a delete-vs-edit case
code_summary: Deterministic field-level three-way merge (equal -> same; base==one side -> take other; both changed -> conflict record with base/local/remote); LWW baseline comparison
expected_behavior: Disjoint edits auto-merge (taxon, note); same-field divergence (height_m 12/15/14) surfaces as an explicit conflict; LWW silently loses the note and one height value; delete-vs-edit flagged
result_stdout_excerpt: merged: taxon 'Fagus orientalis', note 'bark canker seen', height_m '<CONFLICT:height_m>'; conflicts: [{field height_m, base 12, local 15, remote 14}]; W2b LWW present? False False; W2c delete-vs-edit explicit conflict required: True
honest_notes: Demonstrates the contract's shape, not production code quality (e.g. no delete/restore in the merged payload path).
scope_limits: Synthetic JSON toy on three fields; isolated check. Does NOT establish the production merge engine, CRDT/CouchDB-scale behavior, or whole-product merge correctness.

title: Crash/kill recovery harness (V3)
design: Inject SIGKILL at seeded points during save, import and merge in the real app; reopen and assert every record is classified committed/uncommitted/quarantined with no silent loss; verify ops-log chain and commit markers
scope_limits_if_run: Would exercise real storage code; still not proof for arbitrary hardware failure modes

title: Transform round-trip + known-point suite (V1/V2)
design: Forward/inverse round-trip within per-CRS tolerances over the supported CRS list with pinned PROJ; golden-file export byte-stability for identical transform_id; known-point checks against reference coordinates
scope_limits_if_run: Covers only the supported CRS list and pinned versions

title: Merge property tests (V4)
design: Randomized op sequences replicated on two replicas; assert commutativity, idempotence, and no-loss (every non-conflicting change survives; every conflicting change appears in the conflict set)
scope_limits_if_run: Field-level model only; clock/HLC skew cases must be included

title: 250k-observation bounded-access benchmark (V5)
design: Synthetic 250k project; measure viewport p95/p99, FTS search p95, streaming export throughput, peak RSS, cancellation latency on a 4-core/8GB-class machine
scope_limits_if_run: Engineering target validation, not a product-wide performance claim

title: Integrity + license-manifest audit (V6/V7)
design: rtreecheck, ops-log chain verification, blob hash sweep after simulated relocation; assert every bundled tile/source has a license-manifest entry with locator
